title: The 3 A.M. Gas Station Theory: 5 Rules You Must Follow #shorts
description_hook: You pull off an empty highway at 3 A.M. The gas station is open, the fridges hum, and its lights are the only lights for miles.

lines.text: PAY INSIDE. NEVER AT THE PUMP
lines.say: You stop for gas on an empty highway at 3 A.M. Rule one: pay inside, never at the pump.
lines.img: a lonely gas station canopy glowing white under a pitch black sky, empty fuel pumps, an empty highway disappearing into the dark

lines.say: Rule two. Count the cars at the pumps going in. Count again coming out.
lines.img: three dark parked cars beside fuel pumps under harsh canopy lights, no drivers anywhere, wet concrete reflecting the glow

lines.say: Rule three. The coffee is always fresh. Nobody made it.
lines.img: a full glass coffee pot steaming on a warmer in an empty convenience store, humming drink fridges glowing in the background

lines.text: DON'T WAIT FOR THE CLERK TO TURN
lines.say: Rule four. If the clerk faces away, don't wait for him to turn around.
lines.img: a store clerk seen only from behind standing motionless at a counter, facing a back wall of shelves, cold fluorescent light

lines.say: Rule five. Never take the bathroom key on the wooden paddle.
lines.img: a single old metal key hanging from a worn wooden paddle on a hook by a dim side door, flickering light on cracked tiles

lines.say: Drive away. The next station has the same name. And it's 3 A.M. again.
lines.img: the view through a car windshield at night, an empty highway ahead and a familiar glowing gas station canopy appearing in the distance

loop_back: The last line sends the viewer to an identical station at 3 A.M., back to rule one: pay inside.

gumi.say: So. Which rule would you break first?
